question: Two circles of radius of 20 cm each intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. What is the length of the common chord?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two circles of equal **radius (r)** intersect such that each passes through the **centre** of the other, the distance between their centres is equal to the radius **(d = r)**.

Length of the **Common Chord** = √3 × r

Given **r = 20 cm**

Length of common chord = 20 × √3 = 20√3 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of both circles (r) = **20 cm**

Distance between centres (O₁O₂) = **20 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a083826d7154d11aed78f9274a70b3df6e1013d6438928b347257888deda2308.png] 

Let **O₁** and **O₂** be the centres and **AB** be the common chord. Let **M** be the intersection of **O₁O₂** and **AB**.

⇒ O₁O₂ = 20 cm

⇒ O₁M = M O₂ = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm (Line joining centres bisects the common chord at right angles)

⇒ In right-angled triangle **ΔAMO₁**:

⇒ AM² + O₁M² = O₁A²

⇒ AM² + 10² = 20²

⇒ AM² = 400 − 100 = 300

⇒ AM = √300 = 10√3 cm

⇒ Length of common chord **AB = 2 × AM**

⇒ AB = 2 × 10√3 = 20√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Common Chord Formula

Length of common chord L = 2√(r² − (d/2)²), where r is the radius and d is the distance between centres.

Angle in Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always 90°.

Perpendicular from Centre

The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.</p
